prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 公司差旅报销标准 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "费用项目" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "普通员工" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 170px
  col 3: header "经理" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 223px
  col 4: header "总监" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 202px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Define travel-reimbursement limits by expense item and employee grade, so readers can look up their entitlement and compare grades.","reading":"Row-first: identify the expense item in column 1, then scan right across the three grade columns. Column scanning is secondary, for comparing one grade's package. Rows must read as units, and the grade columns must stay directly comparable.","groups":["Columns 2–4 are one peer group: 普通员工, 经理 and 总监 are parallel entitlement levels, so they need comparable widths and alignment.","Column 1 is the row-header key; it should remain visually distinct and readable but not dominate the table."],"keep_intact":["Amount+unit pairs such as 500 元/晚, 350 元/晚, 80 元/日限额 and 120 元/日限额","Fare/class terms 二等座, 一等座 and 经济舱","The number–unit pair 7 天 in 提前 7 天预订","Row labels 一线城市住宿, 其他城市住宿, 高铁, 飞机 and 市内交通"],"may_wrap":["Qualifiers 含早餐, 省会城市可上浮, 需提前 7 天预订 and 可改签一次","The comma-separated second clause in each cell","Longer row labels only in label-compressed designs"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [113, 116, 120, 130] · table 480×358px · row heights [36, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [113, 116, 122, 128] · table 480×381px · row heights [36, 60, 83, 83, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [113, 118, 119, 129] · table 480×358px · row heights [36, 60, 83, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
